title: FreQuant: A Reinforcement-Learning based Adaptive Portfolio Optimization with Multi-frequency Decomposition

problem.claim: Portfolio optimization seeks to allocate assets strategically to maximize returns.

gap.claim: Time-domain portfolio optimization methods may fail to detect sudden market shifts and abrupt events because they are overly tailored to prevalent patterns, causing significant losses.

narrative_sequence.summary: The source asks how inherent frequency features of stock signals can be leveraged for portfolio optimization.
Portfolio optimization is framed as strategic asset allocation intended to maximize returns.
Deep learning and reinforcement learning have been used to capture temporal asset patterns for portfolio optimization.
Time-domain methods can miss sudden market shifts and abrupt events due to overfitting prevalent patterns, resulting in significant losses.

source_observation.claim: Methods focused on prevalent time-domain patterns may fail during sudden market shifts and abrupt events.

interpretation.claim: Representation choices should account for signal characteristics that are not captured by dominant temporal patterns.

application.claim: When designing portfolio optimization systems, evaluate whether the representation can capture frequency-related or abrupt-event information.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish that frequency-based representations improve performance or detect events reliably.

unknowns: The specific proposed method and role of multi-frequency decomposition are not described.
No experiments, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
No explicit author-stated novelty or contribution is supplied.
